subject: Patch propagation & remediation proof-of-process
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire@assuresec.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: security@finledger.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — remediation tempo and patch propagation

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this. As part of FinLedger's SOC 2 readiness review we need evidence of Redwood's vulnerability remediation process specifically around detection -> fix -> propagation across multi-tenant and dedicated fleets. The scope in the CAIQ/SIG asks for: scan cadence, triage SLA, remediation SLA (including exceptions), and a representative closure notice for a medium/high CVE.

Could you provide:
- The formal remediation playbook (PDF) or snapshot of the runbook you follow
- A sample scan snapshot (latest month) showing issue IDs we can correlate to fixes
- A short attestation stating your SLAs (triage time, patch apply window, verification) and how you handle third-party dependencies that require vendor fixes

Also: do you have a documented window for patch propagation (i.e., how long before a fix hits hosted, dedicated, and private deployments)? FinLedger needs this to map to their risk acceptance.

If you can get a draft attestation by EOD tomorrow that would be ideal; we can then schedule a quick follow-up call.

Best,
Claire Park
Senior Assurance Manager
AssureSec LLP
(Attachment: SOC2-Audit-ask-checklist.pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@assuresec.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — remediation tempo and patch propagation

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our remediation playbook and a recent scan snapshot bundle. Quick summary below; I'll loop in Laura for an attestation note and signature.

High-level process (short):
- Continuous scanning: weekly authenticated scans + nightly unauthenticated surface scans. (Scan cadence: weekly auth, nightly unauth)
- Triage SLA: initial severity classification within 72 hours of detection; critical callouts within 24 hours
- Remediation SLA: we target code-level fixes and infra patches to be scheduled within 30 days for applicable internal issues; for critical issues (P0/P1) our goal is fix-and-deploy in <= 7 days with hotfix channels enabled
- Verification: automated regression scans + smoke tests post-deploy; full regression within 7 days of patch rollout
- Propagation windows: hosted API: hotfix typically within 0–6 hours (if critical) or next maintenance window (24–48 hours); Dedicated pools: 24–72 hours depending on node drain/throughput constraints; Private/VPC: deployment cadence depends on customer-managed schedule — we provide signed artifacts and recommended windows (typical recommendation: <30 days for urgent patches)

Third-party dependency exceptions: for vulnerabilities requiring a vendor patch we track the CVE, mark it as vendor-dependent, and apply compensating controls (network egress rules, runtime mitigations) while we monitor vendor timelines. Our exception handling is documented and reviewed weekly; vendor-dependent items have an extended SLA category (90 days) but are escalated to engineering leadership and customers are notified.

Attachments: remediation-playbook-v1.3.pdf, scan-snapshots-202610.zip (contains a collection of Nessus/Trivy/JFrog reports with internal IDs).

Would you accept the 30/7/90 framing (30-day general SLA, 7-day critical, 90-day vendor exception) for the audit? If so I'll get Laura's signed attestation and a sample closure notice (redact customer data) by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: remediation-playbook-v1.3.pdf)

From: Claire Park <claire@assuresec.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: security@finledger.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — remediation tempo and patch propagation

Rishi — that framing works for FinLedger; a couple of clarifications before you escalate for signature:

1) For Dedicated pools: we need a short description of the orchestration steps you take to avoid downtime during node patching (drain strategy, batching window size). A 1–2 paragraph excerpt is fine.
2) For vendor-dependent CVEs: please include one anonymized CVE closure notice that shows the vendor timeline & compensating controls applied (we want to see the notification → mitigations → final closure artifacts)
3) Please include the JIRA or ticket IDs you referenced in your evidence folder so we can cross-check when we review your Drive snapshot

If you can include those in the attestation packet that should close our ask. We can then mark this as satisfied for SOC 2 evidence.

Thanks — Claire
(Attachment: FinLedger-Audit-Schedule.ics)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@assuresec.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — remediation tempo and patch propagation

Hi Claire — attaching a formal attestation and the additional artifacts you requested. Highlights below (this is the statement to be used for SOC 2/CAIQ submission):

Attestation (official):
Redwood Inference confirms the following remediation tempo and handling for vulnerabilities discovered by internal or third-party scanning:
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated scans across production fleet, nightly unauthenticated surface scans, and continuous pipeline SCA checks
- Triage SLA: initial classification within 72 hours, critical issues within 24 hours
- Remediation SLA: critical issues (P0/P1): remediate & verify within 7 calendar days; standard high/medium: target remediation within 30 calendar days; vendor-dependent: tracked as extended SLA up to 90 calendar days and subject to leadership escalation and customer notification
- Verification: automated post-deploy scan + smoke tests; full regression scan within 7 days post-rollout
- Dedicated pool patch propagation: orchestrated drain -> apply -> smoke -> rejoin in batches. Typical batch size: 10–25% of pool per hour, target full propagation in 24–72 hours depending on pool size and customer throughput settings. Detailed runbook excerpt attached.

Provided evidence (attached / Drive):
- remediation-playbook-v1.3.pdf (runbook excerpt including drain strategy and batch sizing)
- scan-snapshots-202610.zip (anonymized scan snapshots; includes internal IDs: RED-SEC-10214, RED-SEC-10255)
- sample-cve-closure-notice.pdf (anonymized example showing vendor timeline, compensating controls, and closure)
- signed-attestation-laura_20261028.pdf (executive-signed attestation)

Representative closure example included shows CVE-2026-3412 (third-party library): vendor notification issued 2026-09-02, exploitability monitored, compensating ingress/egress rules applied 2026-09-04, final vendor patch released 2026-10-14, patch verified and closed in our system 2026-10-18 (JIRA: SEC-4821).

I confirm Redwood will provide ongoing notifications for any customer-impacting vendor-dependent CVEs and will apply compensating controls while awaiting vendor remediation. If FinLedger needs a tailored SLA or different propagation window for private deployments, our account team can coordinate a customer-specific change order.

Links & tickets for your review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-Remediation-Evidence-Oct2026; JIRA SEC-4821.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: signed-attestation-laura_20261028.pdf; sample-cve-closure-notice.pdf)
